verdicts.claim: Every one of the 1,000 duels re-runs, from its receipt, its two cards, the ground and the two signed records, to the very same receipt.
verdicts.saw: 1000 of 1000 duels re-ran to the same receipt

verdicts.claim: Every duel’s batch is 64 distinct GATE rows of its ground, and no duel reads a TEST row.
verdicts.saw: 1000 of 1000 batches were 64 distinct GATE rows with no TEST row

verdicts.claim: All 240 forgeries are refused: an edited challenge, a challenge or acceptance signed by a stranger, an acceptance for another challenge, a stale challenge or acceptance after a give, an edited score, winner or self-play flag in a receipt, a ground of another business, a card fighting itself, an acceptance with an extra field.
The ratings of all the duels, computed twice in their order, are identical, and their total is exactly 1,000 points times the number of rated cards.
verdicts.saw: ratings identical twice; total 341000 over 341 cards

verdicts.claim: In at least 60% of the pairs a majority of five duels decides, the winner is the card with the higher TEST AUC.
verdicts.saw: 156 of 199 decided pairs (78.4%): the majority winner had the higher TEST AUC

verdicts.claim: At least 10% of the decided duels are won by the card with the lower GATE AUC: a duel is a fight, not a lookup of the two scores.
verdicts.saw: 261 of 994 decided duels (26.3%) were won by the card with the lower GATE AUC

verdicts.claim: The median duel takes at most 250 milliseconds on the measuring machine, signatures included.
